name: Information Security Fundamentals
summary: The vocabulary and the mindset of the field: what risk is, what defence in depth is and why trust is the problem.
prerequisites: No programming required. It is the entry point of both security tracks.
syllabus: The CIA triad and what it guides in practice
Zero Trust: never trust, always verify
Standards and frameworks: ISO, NIST, CIS, CSF and RMF

topics.title: The CIA triad: confidentiality, integrity and availability
Defining risk: threat, vulnerability and impact
Assessing and treating risk: accept, mitigate, transfer or avoid
Defence in depth: layers that hold each other up
The idea of isolation and least privilege
Zero Trust: principles and what changes in the architecture
Authentication and authorisation: the difference everyone confuses
Blue, red and purple teams: roles and cooperation
False positive, false negative, true positive and true negative
Backups, resilience and testing your restores
The role of compliance and of auditors
The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) and the RMF
Brazil’s LGPD and the duty to protect personal data
Careers in the field: SOC, pentest, GRC, forensics and AppSec
